name: Ethiopia

facts.religion: Orthodox Christian about 43%, Muslim about 34%, Protestant about 19%

system_note: A federation of ethnically defined regions.
snapshot: Abiy Ahmed's party swept a June 2026 election held amid a crackdown; by October war had returned to Tigray, and federal forces retook Mekelle and pushed to the Eritrean border.
culture: Ethiopia was never colonised, apart from a brief Italian occupation, and has its own calendar, its own script and one of the world's oldest Christian churches, whose rock-hewn churches at Lalibela still hold services. Coffee was first drunk here, and the coffee ceremony is a daily social ritual. Ethiopian distance runners are national heroes, and Amharic, Oromo and Tigrinya music fills Addis Ababa's bars.
society: With some 135 million people, Ethiopia is Africa's second most populous country. State-led growth built roads, industrial parks and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, inaugurated in 2025 over Egypt's objections. The 2020 to 2022 Tigray war killed hundreds of thousands. Inflation and a 2024 currency float have squeezed households.
situation: In 2019, Abiy Ahmed won the Nobel Peace Prize for ending a 20-year standoff with Eritrea. A year later he went to war in Tigray, a conflict that killed hundreds of thousands, with Eritrean troops fighting on his side. In 2026 he won another election, and the former partners in that war were edging toward a new one against each other.

Abiy's Prosperity Party won 438 seats in the 1 June parliamentary election, nearly 90 percent, amid what AP called a crackdown on dissent, with his most prominent critics jailed, exiled or missing (AP via WSPA). Some 143 polling stations never opened because of fighting in Amhara and Oromia, where insurgencies continue (AFP via Africanews). In Tigray, the TPLF restored its pre-war administration just before the vote, pushing aside an interim government Abiy had appointed. Abiy has also repeatedly said landlocked Ethiopia, with 130 million people, must regain access to the Red Sea, which it lost when Eritrea became independent in 1993; Eritrea calls that imperial ambition and Addis Ababa accuses Asmara of arming rebels (Rainbow Radio). The economy grows fast on construction and coffee, yet 43 percent of Ethiopians live in poverty. Parliament is due to re-elect Abiy this month.
power: A federal parliamentary republic of ethnically defined regions. The prime minister, chosen by the House of Peoples' Representatives, holds executive power; the president is ceremonial. In practice the Prosperity Party dominates.
holders: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (Prosperity Party), in office since 2018.

update.html: War returned to Tigray in late September. After the TPLF and allied armed groups attacked from about 22 September, federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force retook Mekelle in early October, then Shire, Adigrat, Adwa and Axum, and reached the Eritrean border at Zalambessa. Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties on 1 October; Eritrean troops pulled back from Adigrat but stayed dug in around Zalambessa and Badme. Addis Ababa has put Tigray under six months of federal interim rule, while Fano keeps attacking supply lines in Amhara.
